sources.title: Laya — 33ms Multilingual System 1 Decision Engine
sources.snippet: Instead of staying bitter, I decided to take everything I learned, fix every architectural limitation of the old approach, and build a completely open, horizontal System 1 decision model family: Laya.

sources.title: Laya - Open Typed Decisions with Calibrated Probabilities | AI/TLDR
sources.snippet: Laya sits in the structured-output layer alongside SemIf and the constrained-decoding libraries such as Outlines and XGrammar. The difference is the same one SemIf draws: those tools shape the tokens a generative model emits, while Laya replaces generation entirely for the narrow case of scoring a fixed set of described options.

sources.title: Laya AI — System One Decision Model
sources.snippet: Laya AI · System One Laya AI — System One Decision Model Typed decisions for agents and software — choice, score, and yes/no in one forward pass. Hosted prepaid API here; Apache 2.0 weights if you run locally.

sources.title: Laya - 512 context, open source | LLM Reference
sources.snippet: Laya is ConvAI Innovations' English open-weight System 1 decision model (ModernBERT-large, 421M, context 512), released on Hugging Face on 2026-09-18 under Apache 2.0. It is non-autoregressive: a state plus typed questions (choice, score, or noul) returns calibrated probabilities in one forward pass, trained with RLCD, and it does not generate text.
